paragraphs: Franklin BSP Realty Trust, Inc. (the "Company"), is a real estate finance company, formed as a Maryland corporation, that has elected to be treated as a real estate investment trust ("REIT") for U.S. federal income tax purposes since 2013. Substantially all of the Company's business is conducted through FBRT OP LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the "OP") and to its subsidiaries. The Company is the managing member of the OP and directly or indirectly held 91% of the common units of membership interests in the OP as of December 31, 2025.

As discussed in more detail below, the Company's operations are organized into two business units: (i) Commercial Real Estate Financing, and (ii) Agency Business. On July 1, 2025, through a wholly owned subsidiary, the Company acquired NewPoint Holdings JV LLC ("NewPoint"), which now comprises the Company's Agency Business unit.

The Company is externally managed by Benefit Street Partners L.L.C. (the "Advisor") pursuant to an advisory agreement, as amended on August 18, 2021 (the "Advisory Agreement"). The Advisor manages our affairs on a day-to-day basis. The Advisor receives compensation and fees for services related to the investment and management of our assets and our operations. Established in 2008, the Advisor's credit platform manages funds for institutions and high-net-worth investors across various credit funds and complementary strategies including high yield, levered loans, private/opportunistic debt, liquid credit, structured credit and commercial real estate debt. These strategies complement each other as they all leverage the sourcing, analytical, compliance, and operational capabilities that encompass the platform. The Advisor is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Franklin Resources, Inc., which together with its various subsidiaries operates as "Franklin Templeton."
As of December 31, 2025, we had 223 employees, all of which are employees of NewPoint.
Our objective is to provide our common shareholders attractive, risk-adjusted returns through dividends and capital growth.
The Company's operations are organized into two business units: (i) Commercial Real Estate Financing, and (ii) Agency Business.

The Commercial Real Estate Financing business unit primarily focuses on originating, acquiring and asset managing commercial real estate debt investments, including first mortgage loans, subordinated mortgage loans, mezzanine loans and participations in such loans. Secondarily, this unit also invests in and asset manages real estate securities, with a historical focus on commercial mortgage-backed securities ("CMBS"), commercial real estate collateralized loan obligation bonds and single asset single borrower bonds (collectively "CMBS bonds"), collateralized debt obligations ("CDOs") and other securities. Through this unit the Company also originates conduit loans which the Company intends to sell through its taxable REIT subsidiary ("TRS") into CMBS securitization transactions, and owns real estate that was either acquired by the Company through foreclosure, deed-in-lieu of foreclosure or that was purchased for investment. These financing activities are described in additional detail below.

We originate, fund, acquire and structure commercial real estate debt, including first mortgage loans, mezzanine loans, bridge loans, and other loans related to commercial real estate. We may also acquire some equity participations in the underlying collateral of commercial real estate debt. We structure, underwrite, and originate most of our investments. We use conservative underwriting criteria to focus on risk adjusted returns based on several factors, which may include the leverage point, debt service coverage and sensitivity, lease sustainability studies, market and economic conditions, quality of the underlying collateral and location, reputation and track record of the borrower, and a clear exit or refinancing plan for the borrower. Our underwriting process involves comprehensive financial, structural, operational, and legal due diligence to assess any risks in connection with making such investments so that we can optimize pricing and structuring. By originating loans directly, we are able to structure and underwrite loans that satisfy our standards, establish a direct relationship with the borrower, and utilize our own preferred documentation. Described below are some of the types of loans we may originate or acquire. In addition, although we generally prefer the benefits of new origination, market conditions can create situations where holders of commercial real estate debt may be in distress and are therefore willing to sell to us at prices that compensate us for the lack of control typically associated with directly structured investments.

We primarily focus on first mortgage loans. First mortgage loans generally finance the acquisition, refinancing or rehabilitation of commercial real estate. First mortgage loans may be either short (one-to-five years) or long (up to ten years) term, may be fixed or floating rate, and are predominantly current-pay loans. We may originate or acquire current-pay first mortgage loans backed by properties that fit our investment strategy. We may selectively syndicate portions of these loans, including senior or junior participations that will effectively provide permanent financing or optimize returns which may include retained origination fees.

First mortgage loans typically provide for a higher recovery rate and lower defaults than other debt positions due to the lender's favorable control position, which at times can include control of the entire capital structure. Because of these attributes, this type of investment typically receives favorable treatment from third-party rating agencies and financing sources, which should increase the liquidity of these investments. However, these loans typically generate lower returns than subordinate debt, such as subordinate loans and mezzanine loans, commonly referred to as B-notes.

B-notes consist of subordinate mortgage loans, including structurally subordinated first mortgage loans and junior participations in first mortgage loans or participations in these types of assets. Like first mortgage loans, these loans generally finance the acquisition, refinancing, rehabilitation or construction of commercial real estate. Subordinated mortgage loans or B-notes may be either short (one-to-five years) or long (up to ten years) term, may be fixed or floating rate, and are predominantly current-pay loans. We may originate or acquire current-pay subordinated mortgage loans or B-notes backed by high quality properties that fit our investment strategy. We may create subordinated mortgage loans by tranching our directly originated first mortgage loans generally through syndications of senior first mortgages or we may buy such assets directly from third party originators.

We may offer bridge financing products to borrowers who are typically seeking short-term capital to be used in an acquisition, development or refinancing of a given property. From the borrower's perspective, shorter term bridge financing is advantageous because it allows time to improve the property value through repositioning without encumbering it with restrictive long-term debt. The terms of these loans generally do not exceed three years.

Mezzanine loans are secured by one or more direct or indirect ownership interests in an entity that directly or indirectly owns commercial real estate and generally finance the acquisition, refinancing, rehabilitation or construction of commercial real estate. Mezzanine loans may be either short (one-to-five years) or long (up to ten years) term and may be fixed or floating rate. We may originate or acquire mezzanine loans backed by properties that fit our investment strategy. We may own such mezzanine loans directly or we may hold a participation in a mezzanine loan or a sub-participation in a mezzanine loan. These loans are predominantly current-pay loans (although there may be a portion of the interest that accrues) and may provide for participation in the value or cash flow appreciation of the underlying property as described below. With the credit market disruption and resulting dearth of capital available in this part of the capital structure, we believe that the opportunities to both directly originate and to buy mezzanine loans from third parties on favorable terms will continue to be attractive.

We may pursue equity participation opportunities in connection with our commercial real estate debt originations if we believe that the risk-reward characteristics of the loan merit additional upside participation related to the potential appreciation in value of the underlying assets securing the loan. Equity participations can be paid in the form of additional interest, exit fees, percentage of sharing in refinance or resale proceeds or warrants in the borrower. Equity participation can also take the form of a conversion feature, sometimes referred to as a "kicker," which permits the lender to convert a loan or preferred equity investment into common equity in the borrower at a negotiated premium to the current net asset value of the borrower. We expect to generate additional revenues from any equity participations in which we invest as a result of excess cash flows being distributed or as appreciated properties are sold or refinanced.

headings: Risk Related to Our Financing Strategy
We have a significant amount of indebtedness and may need to incur more in the future.
We may not be able to earn returns on loans we make in excess of the interest we pay on our borrowings.
We may use collateralized debt and loan obligation securitization markets to provide long-term financing for our loans and investments which may not be available.
Lenders often require us to enter into restrictive covenants relating to our operations, which could limit our ability to make distributions.
Changes in interest rates, particularly short-term interest rates, may significantly influence our net income.

We may not be able to access financing sources on attractive terms, if at all, which could adversely affect our ability to fund and grow our business, or result in dilution to our existing stockholders.

Our short-term borrowings often require us to provide additional collateral when the fair market value of our collateral decreases, and these calls for collateral could significantly impact our liquidity position.
Risks Related to Our Investments
Our commercial real estate debt investments are subject to the risks typically associated with ownership of commercial real estate.
Loans on properties in transition will involve a greater risk of loss than conventional mortgage loans.
Our success depends on the availability of attractive investment opportunities.
Delays in liquidating defaulted commercial real estate debt investments could reduce our investment returns.
Operating and disposing of properties acquired through foreclosure subject us to additional risks that could harm our results of operations.
Subordinate commercial real estate debt that we originate or acquire could expose us to greater losses than primary mortgage loans do.
We may be subject to risks associated with construction lending, such as declining real estate values, cost overruns and delays in completion.
Insurance may not cover all potential losses on the properties underlying our investments, which may harm the value of our assets.
We invest in CMBS and CMBS bonds, which entails certain risks, including those related to subordinate securities.

We may not control the special servicing of the mortgage loans underlying the CMBS and CMBS bonds in which we invest and, in such cases, the special servicer may take actions that could adversely affect our interests.
We invest in CDOs and such investments involve significant risks.
Most of our investments are illiquid and we may not be able to vary our portfolio in response to changes in economic and other conditions, which may result in losses to us.
Some of our investments are carried at estimated fair value as determined by us and, as a result, there may be uncertainty as to the value of these investments.
Competition with third parties for originating and acquiring investments may reduce our profitability.
Our due diligence may not reveal all material issues relating to our origination or acquisition of a particular investment.
We may be unable to restructure loans in a manner that we believe maximizes value, particularly if we are one of multiple creditors in large capital structures.
We may be subject to risks associated with future advance obligations, such as declining real estate values and operating performance.
We may not be successful in our attempts to align the maturities of our liabilities with the maturities on our assets, which could harm our operating results and financial condition.
Provision for credit losses is difficult to estimate.
Any credit ratings assigned to our investments will be subject to ongoing evaluations and revisions and we cannot assure you that those ratings will not be downgraded.

When we acquire companies, we face risks related to integrating the acquired company in a manner that allows us to achieve the synergies and other benefits of the acquisition or do so within the anticipated time frame.
Risks Related to the Conduit Segment of the Business
We use warehouse facilities that may limit our ability to acquire assets, and we may incur losses if the collateral is liquidated.
We directly and indirectly utilize non‑recourse securitizations, and such structures expose us to risks that could result in losses to us.
The securitization market is subject to a regulatory environment that may affect certain aspects of these activities.
We enter into hedging transactions that could expose us to contingent liabilities in the future.
Hedging against interest rate exposure may adversely affect our income, limit our gains or result in losses, which could adversely affect cash available for distribution to our stockholders.
Risks Related to NewPoint and our Agency Business

The acquisition of NewPoint and the operation of our Agency Business exposes us to a variety of additional risks that could materially and adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
Risks Related to Conflicts of Interest

The Advisor faces conflicts of interest relating to purchasing commercial real estate-related investments, and such conflicts may not be resolved in our favor, which could adversely affect our investment opportunities.
The Advisor and its employees face competing demands relating to their time, and this may cause our operating results to suffer.
The fee structure set forth in the Advisory Agreement may not create proper incentives for the Advisor.
Termination of our Advisory Agreement would be difficult and costly.
Risks Related to Our Corporate Structure
The limit on the number of shares a person may own may discourage a takeover that could otherwise result in a premium price to our stockholders.

In connection with executing our business strategies, we expect to evaluate the possibility of originating, funding, and acquiring additional commercial real estate debt and making other strategic investments, and we may elect to finance these endeavors by incurring additional indebtedness. The amount of such indebtedness could have material adverse consequences, including:
•hindering our ability to adjust to changing market, industry or economic conditions;
•limiting our ability to access the capital markets to raise additional equity or refinance maturing debt on favorable terms or fund acquisitions;
•limiting the amount of cash flow available for future operations, acquisitions, dividends, stock repurchases or other uses;
•making us more vulnerable to economic or industry downturns, including interest rate increases or sustained high interest rate environments; and
•placing us at a competitive disadvantage compared to less leveraged competitors.

Through this unit the Company also originates conduit loans which the Company intends to sell through its TRS into CMBS securitization transactions, and owns real estate that was either acquired by the Company through foreclosure, deed-in-lieu of foreclosure or that was purchased for investment.

Through this unit, we originate, sell and service a range of multifamily finance products under programs offered by government-sponsored enterprises ("GSEs"), such as the Federal National Mortgage Association ("Fannie Mae") and Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation ("Freddie Mac") and by government agencies ("Agencies"), such as the Government National Mortgage Association ("Ginnie Mae") and the Federal Housing Administration, a division of the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (together with Ginnie Mae, "HUD"). We retain the servicing rights and asset management responsibilities on substantially all loans we originate and sell under the GSE and HUD programs. We are an approved Fannie Mae Delegated Underwriting and Servicing ("DUS") lender, a Freddie Mac Program Plus Seller/Servicer, a Multifamily Accelerated Processing ("MAP") and Section 232 LEAN lender for HUD and a Ginnie Mae issuer. paragraphs: Franklin BSP Realty Trust, Inc. (the "Company"), 是一家房地產金融公司，成立為馬裏蘭州公司，自2013年起已選擇被視為美國聯邦所得稅用途的房地產投資信託 ("REIT")。本公司業務幾乎全部透過FBRT OP LLC，一家特拉華州有限責任公司 (the "OP") 及其子公司進行。本公司為OP的管理成員，並於2025年12月31日持有OP普通單位權益的91%。
如後文更詳細說明，本公司業務分為兩個業務單位：(i) 商業不動產融資，以及 (ii) 代理業務。2025年7月1日，本公司透過 wholly owned subsidiary 收購 NewPoint Holdings JV LLC ("NewPoint")，此後即組成本公司代理業務單位。

本公司由 Benefit Street Partners L.L.C. (the "Advisor") 外部管理，根據2021年8月18日簽訂的 (the "Advisory Agreement") 委託協議進行管理。Advisor 負責本公司日常業務的運作。Advisor 會因投資及管理本公司資產與運作之服務收取報酬與費用。Advisor 於2008年成立，其信用平台管理機構與高淨值投資者之資金，涵蓋多種信用基金與補充策略，包括高收益債券、槓桿貸款、私人/機會性貸款、流動性信用、結構性信用與商業不動產貸款。這些策略彼此補充，因它們皆運用平台的來源、分析、合規與運作能力。Advisor 是 Franklin Resources, Inc. 的 wholly-owned subsidiary，與其各子公司共同運作為 "Franklin Templeton."
截至2025年12月31日，本公司共有223名員工，皆為NewPoint之員工。
本公司目標是透過股息與資本成長，為普通股東提供具吸引力且風險調整後的回報。
本公司業務分為兩個業務單位：(i) 商業不動產融資，以及 (ii) 代理業務。

商業不動產融資業務單位主要專注於發起、取得與管理商業不動產貸款投資，包括首優先抵押貸款、次級抵押貸款、Mezzanine貸款與參與貸款。次要地，此單位也投資與管理不動產證券，歷史上專注於商業抵押貸款支持證券 ("CMBS")、商業不動產擔保貸款義務債券與單一資產單一借款人債券 (合稱 "CMBS bonds")、擔保債務義務 ("CDOs") 及其他證券。透過此單位，本公司也發起 conduit loans，並計畫透過本公司稅務負擔REIT子公司 ("TRS") 售出至CMBS證券化交易，並擁有透過拍賣、債務抵償或購入投資取得的不動產。這些融資活動於後文有更詳細說明。

我們發起、資金、取得與結構商業不動產貸款，包括首優先抵押貸款、Mezzanine貸款、橋樑貸款與其他與商業不動產相關貸款。我們也可能取得部分商業不動產貸款之權益參與。我們結構、承銷與發起大多數投資。我們使用保守的承銷標準，專注於基於多種因素的風險調整回報，這些因素可能包括槓桿點、債務覆蓋率與敏感度、租賃永續性研究、市場與總體經濟條件、基礎資產品質與地點、借款人聲譽與履歷，以及借款人明確的退出或再融資計畫。我們的承銷程序包含全面的財務、結構、運作與法律盡職調查，以評估與此投資相關的風險，使我們能優化價格與結構。透過直接發起貸款，我們能結構與承銷符合我們標準的貸款，與借款人建立直接關係，並使用我們自己的優先文件。後文說明我們可能發起或取得的一些貸款類型。此外，雖然我們通常偏好新發起的優點，但市場條件可能導致商業不動產貸款持有人陷入困境，因此願意以補償我們缺乏直接結構投資控制權的價格出售給我們。

我們主要著重於第一順位抵押貸款。第一順位抵押貸款通常用以資助商業不動產的取得、重新貸款或翻修。第一順位抵押貸款可能是短期（一至五年）或長期（最多十年），可能是固定利率或浮動利率，且多為現金償還貸款。我們可能發行或取得符合我們投資策略的現金償還第一順位抵押貸款，這些貸款可能由符合我們投資策略的不動產擔保。我們可能選擇性地將這些貸款的部分 syndicate，包括高階或低階參與，這些參與將有效提供永久性融資或優化回報，可能包含保留的發行手續費。
第一順位抵押貸款通常提供較高的回收率與較低的違約率，這是因為貸款人擁有較有利的控制地位，有時甚至包括對整個資本結構的控制。由於這些特質，這種投資類型通常會獲得第三方評級機構與融資來源的優待，這應該會增加這些投資的流動性。然而，這些貸款通常產生的回報率低於次級貸款，例如次級貸款與 Mezzanine 貸款，常被稱為 B-notes。

B-notes 組成次級抵押貸款，包括結構上次級的第一順位抵押貸款與第一順位抵押貸款的低階參與或這些類型資產的參與。與第一順位抵押貸款一樣，這些貸款通常用以資助商業不動產的取得、重新貸款、翻修或建設。次級抵押貸款或 B-notes 可能是短期（一至五年）或長期（最多十年），可能是固定利率或浮動利率，且多為現金償還貸款。我們可能發行或取得符合我們投資策略的現金償還次級抵押貸款或 B-notes，這些貸款由符合我們投資策略的高品質不動產擔保。我們可能透過高階第一順位抵押貸款的 syndication 來創造次級抵押貸款，或直接從第三方發行者購買這些資產。
我們可能為尋求短期資金以用於特定不動產的取得、開發或重新貸款的借款人提供橋樑貸款產品。從借款人的觀點來看，較短的橋樑貸款期限是有利的，因為這允許時間改善不動產價值，透過重新定位而不必負擔限制性的長期債務。這些貸款的期限通常不超過三年。

Mezzanine 貸款以一個或多個直接或間接擁有商業不動產的實體的直接或間接所有權權益為擔保，通常用以資助商業不動產的取得、重新貸款、翻修或建設。Mezzanine 貸款可能是短期（一至五年）或長期（最多十年），可能是固定利率或浮動利率。我們可能發行或取得符合我們投資策略的 Mezzanine 貸款。我們可能直接擁有這些 Mezzanine 貸款，或持有 Mezzanine 貸款的參與或次參與。這些貸款多為現金償還貸款（雖然可能有部分利息累計），並可能提供參與基礎不動產價值或現金流增值的權利，如下列所述。由於信貸市場的動盪與此資本結構中可用資金的減少，我們認為在有利條件下直接發行或從第三方購買 Mezzanine 貸款的機會將持續具有吸引力。

我們可能在商業不動產貸款發行時尋求股權參與機會，如果我們認為貸款的風險回報特性值得額外參與，以獲得基礎資產價值增值的潛在收益。股權參與可以以附加利息、退出費用、重組或出售所得的百分比分享或借款人股權的選擇權形式支付。股權參與也可以以轉換特權的形式出現，有時稱為「kicker」，這允許貸款人將貸款或優先股權投資轉換為借款人的普通股，價格為借款人當前淨資產價值的協議 premium。我們預期會因投資的股權參與而產生額外收入，原因可能是過剩現金流的分配，或是資產價值上升後的出售或重新貸款。

paragraphs: 以下討論與分析應配合閱讀本公司 Franklin BSP Realty Trust, Inc. 附屬之財務報表、相關附註及其他財務資訊，這些資訊包含於本年度 Form 10-K 申報書其他部分。
herein 所稱 "the Company," "we," "our" 以及 "us" 指的是 Franklin BSP Realty Trust, Inc.，為馬裏蘭州公司，並根據語境，亦指 FBRT OP LLC，為特拉華州有限責任公司，我們稱之為 "OP"，以及其子公司。本公司由 Benefit Street Partners L.L.C.（我們的 "Advisor"）外部管理。
本討論包含前瞻性陳述，反映本公司目前對可能影響我們未來營運結果或財務狀況的事件與財務趨勢的預期、估計與假設。實際結果與事件的時間點可能與這些前瞻性陳述所載內容有重大差異，原因包括在本年度 Form 10-K 申報書 "Risk Factors"（風險因素）與 "Forward-Looking Statements"（前瞻性陳述）部分所討論的多種因素。
本公司為馬裏蘭州公司，自 2013 年起已就稅務選項申報為美國聯邦所得稅用途的不動產投資信託（"REIT"）。我們業務的 substantially all 皆透過 OP 進行，為特拉華州有限責任公司。我們為 OP 的管理成員，並於 2025 年 12 月 31 日持有 OP 會員權益普通單位的 91%。

本公司的營運分為兩個業務單位：(i) 商業不動產融資，以及 (ii) 代理業務。商業不動產融資單位主要專注於發起、取得及管理商業不動產債務投資，包括首優先抵押貸款、次級抵押貸款、Mezzanine 貸款及參與貸款。次要地，此單位亦投資並管理不動產證券，歷史上專注於商業抵押貸款支持證券（"CMBS"）、商業不動產擔保貸款義務債券及單一資產單一借款人債券（合稱 "CMBS 債券"）、擔保債務義務（"CDOs"）及其他證券。透過此單位，本公司亦發起 conduit 貸款，並有意透過 TRS 売出至 CMBS 資產證券化交易，並擁有透過拍賣、債務代償或投資購入的不動產。

2025 年 7 月 1 日，透過 wholly owned 子公司，我們取得 NewPoint Holdings JV LLC（"NewPoint"），此後即為我們的代理業務單位。透過此單位，我們發起、銷售並管理一系列多戶住宅金融產品，這些產品透過政府支持企業（"GSEs"）提供的方案，例如美國聯邦住宅貸款銀行（"Fannie Mae"）與美國房屋貸款公司（"Freddie Mac"），以及政府機構（"Agencies"）提供的方案，例如美國政府住宅抵押貸款協會（"Ginnie Mae"）與美國住房及都市發展部的住房管理局（"HUD"）。我們保留對透過 GSE 與 HUD 方案發起並銷售的貸款的服務權與資產管理責任。我們為 Fannie Mae 的授權貸款人與服務機構（"DUS"）、Freddie Mac 的 Program Plus 賣家與服務機構，為 HUD 的多戶住宅加速處理（"MAP"）與第 232 節 LEAN 貸款人，並為 Ginnie Mae 發行者。此外，本公司亦服務外部的商業不動產融資產品組合。
本公司由 Advisor 管理，根據 2021 年 8 月 18 日簽訂的 "Advisory Agreement"（"諮詢協議"）。Advisor 依據此協議管理我們的日常業務。Advisor 獲得與投資及管理我們資產與營運相關的報酬與費用。

Advisor 為 SEC 登記的投資顧問，為一專注於信貸的另類資產管理公司。Advisor 管理機構與高淨值投資者的多種信貸基金與補充策略，包括高收益債券、槓桿貸款、私人/機會性貸款、流動信貸、結構化信貸與商業不動產貸款。這些策略相互補充，因它們皆運用 Advisor 強大的平台所具備的來源、分析、合規與運營能力。Advisor 為 Franklin Resources, Inc. 的 wholly-owned 子公司，與其各子公司共同運作為 "Franklin Templeton"。
截至2025年12月31日，本公司共有223名員工，皆為NewPoint之員工。

headings: 與我們融資策略相關的風險
我們擁有相當程度的負債，未來可能需要增加更多負債。
我們可能無法從貸款所產生的回報中，獲得超過我們支付借款利息的收益。
我們可能利用擔保債務及貸款義務證券化市場，為我們的貸款及投資提供長期融資，但這些融資可能無法取得。
貸款人經常要求我們訂立限制性契約，限制我們的營運，這可能會限制我們發放紅利的能力。
利率的變動，特別是短期利率的變動，可能會顯著影響我們的淨收入。
我們可能無法以有吸引力的條件取得融資來源，甚至無法取得，這可能會不利於我們資助並成長業務的能力，或導致現有股東的股權稀釋。
我們的短期借款通常需要在擔保品的公平市價下降時，提供額外擔保品，這些擔保品的要求可能會顯著影響我們的流動性地位。
與我們投資相關的風險
我們的商業不動產貸款投資會面臨通常與擁有商業不動產相關的風險。
位於轉型中的不動產上的貸款會比傳統的房貸有更高的虧損風險。
我們的成功取決於有吸引人的投資機會。
延遲處置違約的商業不動產貸款投資可能會降低我們的投資回報。
取得財產後的營運與處置會使我們面臨額外的風險，這些風險可能影響我們的營運成果。
我們所發行或取得的次級商業不動產貸款可能會使我們面臨比主要房貸更高的損失風險。
我們可能面臨與建築貸款相關的風險，例如不動產價值下跌、成本超支以及完工延誤。
保險可能無法涵蓋我們投資之不動產所產生之所有潛在損失，此情形可能影響我們資產之價值。
我們投資於CMBS及CMBS債券，此類投資包含某些風險，包括與次級證券相關之風險。
我們可能無法控制我們投資之CMBS及CMBS債券所背後之房貸貸款之特別服務，於此情況下，特別服務機構可能採取對我們權益產生不利影響之行動。
我們投資於CDOs，此類投資涉及重大風險。
我們絕大多數之投資為非流動性，我們可能無法根據經濟及其他條件之變動調整投資組合，此情形可能導致我們產生損失。
我們部分投資以我們所評估之公允價值計入，因此這些投資之價值可能存在不確定性。
我們與第三方競爭發起及取得投資，可能降低我們之盈利能力。
我們之盡職調查可能無法揭露與我們發起或取得特定投資相關之所有重大問題。
我們可能無法以我們認為能最大化價值的方式重新安排貸款，特別是在我們是大型資本結構中多個債權人之一的情況下。
我們可能面臨未來預付款義務相關的風險，例如不動產價值下降及營運表現惡化。
我們可能無法成功地將我們的負債到期日與我們的資產到期日對應，這可能會影響我們的營運結果與財務狀況。
信貸損失備抵提列難以準確預估。
任何針對我們投資之信用評等，將會持續進行評估與修正，我們無法保證這些評等不會被降級。
當我們取得公司時，我們面臨整合取得公司的方式，以達成併購的協同效益及其他好處，或在預期時間內完成的風險。
與業務之 conduit 分部相關的風險
我們使用倉庫設施，可能限制我們取得資產的能力，且若質押物被清算，我們可能產生損失。
本公司直接及間接使用非 recourse 拆分融資，且此等結構可能使本公司面臨導致本公司產生損失的風險。
拆分融資市場受制於監管環境，可能影響這些活動的某些方面。
本公司進行避險交易，可能使本公司未來面臨潛在負債。
對利率風險進行避險可能不利於本公司收入，限制本公司獲利或導致損失，這可能會不利於本公司用以分配給股東的現金。
與 NewPoint 及本公司代理業務相關的風險
收購 NewPoint 及經營本公司代理業務使本公司面臨多種額外風險，這些風險可能對本公司財務狀況及營運成果造成重大且不利的影響。
與利益衝突相關的風險
顧問面臨與購買商業不動產相關投資的利益衝突，且這些衝突可能無法對本公司有利，這可能會不利於本公司投資機會。
The Advisor 以及其員工面臨時間上的競爭需求，這可能會導致我們的營運結果受損。
Advisory Agreement 中所規定的費用結構可能無法為 Advisor 創造適當的動機。
我們的 Advisory Agreement 終止將會困難且成本高昂。
與我們公司結構相關的風險
個人所能擁有的股票數量上限可能會阻卻一場 takeover，而該 takeover 可能會導致股東獲得較高的股票價格。

paragraphs: 我們擁有相當程度的負債。在執行我們的業務策略時，我們預期會評估發起、融資及取得額外商業不動產貸款以及進行其他戰略投資的可能性，並可能選擇透過增加負債來資金融通這些業務。此類負債的金額可能會產生重大不利後果，包括：
• 妨礙我們調整以應對變動中的市場、產業或經濟條件；
• 限制我們進入資本市場以籌措額外股本或以有利條件重新融資到期債務或資助收購的能力；
• 限制未來營運、收購、股息、股票回購或其他用途可用的現金流量；
• 讓我們更容易受到經濟或產業衰退的影響，包括利率上升或持續高利率環境；以及
• 讓我們相較於負債較低的競爭對手處於競爭劣勢。
